title: Book Three · Chapter 72: The Usual Envelope
story:
That evening, Dad puts his usual household money beside Mum's work sheet.

Mum has her own earnings in another envelope. She counts the two amounts, writes a short line, and puts some aside for cloth and thread.

Ronan comes in with his little Saturday payment.

For a moment, he holds it near the table. Then he looks at the two larger envelopes.

“Do you need this too?” he asks.

Mum looks up.

“Your delivery money?”

He nods.

Dad moves a chair back so Ronan can sit.

“Keep it,” Mum says. “We put aside the house money first. Your trips helped me finish work.”

Ronan sits down. He turns one coin between his fingers.

“I could buy the bread tomorrow.”

Dad smiles. “We can eat that.”

“For everyone,” Ronan says.

“Then not only the small sweet one.”

Mum laughs. She puts away her work sheet and takes a folded paper from the shelf.

It is a note from her friend. They want to look at cloth together next week. Mum has marked one afternoon with a circle.

Dad asks about a piece for her own bag.

“The bag is fine,” she says. “This is for a cushion. Mine.”

“I won't ask to carry it to work.”

“Good.”

Ronan laughs. He puts the bread money in his pocket and the rest in his own envelope.

Dad takes out a small list of things he needs for work. One item costs more than he wants to spend this week. He draws a line under it and leaves it for later.

Ronan looks at the list.

“Not all now?”

“Not all now. I have the old one for a little longer.”

Dad folds the list and puts it with his work bag. Then he goes to wash the rice bowl.

Mum brings a small piece of dark cloth to the lamp. She checks its colour beside a lighter one.

“For the cushion?” Ronan asks.

“One idea.”

He looks at the two pieces. “The dark one.”

Mum moves them around and looks again. “Maybe.”

She makes her own choice and puts the cloth away. Ronan does not see which she keeps on top.

Outside, someone pushes a cart past the green door. Dad comes back with damp hands and reaches for the towel.

“Bread early?” he asks.

“Before breakfast.”

“A good time for it.”

Ronan leaves the small coins beside his coat. He sets his gloves on the chair too. Tomorrow's first errand will be a short walk for warm bread, with no coat bag to carry.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

earnings＝劳动收入；amount＝数额；cushion＝靠垫、坐垫；item＝一项物品。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan的小额报酬是不是全家收入的主要来源？父母怎样安排自己的钱？
2. 他自愿答应了哪件小事？Mum和Dad又各有什么自己的计划？

## 读句子

**He turns one coin between his fingers.**

拆开看：He / turns one coin / between his fingers.

他／转动一枚硬币／在手指之间。
